subject: general
question: How much will a sum of ₹60,000 become after one year if the interest is compounded half-yearly at 18% per annum compound interest?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For **half-yearly compounding**, the rate becomes half and the number of periods doubles.

Rate (r) = 18% ÷ 2 = 9% per half-year | Time (n) = 1 × 2 = 2 periods.

**Net effective interest rate** for 2 periods = 9 + 9 + (9 × 9)/100 = 18.81%.

Total Amount = 100% (Principal) + 18.81% (Interest) = 118.81% of Principal.

Amount = 60,000 × 1.1881 = ₹71,286.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹71,286.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Principal (P) = **₹60,000**

Annual Rate (R) = **18% per annum**

Time (T) = **1 year**

**Formula Used:**

Amount (A) = P(1 + r/100)ⁿ

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/dc51a4c2eb74e22dac212cc8bfc8a5fc9855608e40c922496515aa7a4a0281e1.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ r = 18 ÷ 2 = 9% (Rate for 6 months)

⇒ n = 1 × 2 = 2 (Two half-year periods in 1 year)

⇒ A = 60,000 × (1 + 9/100)²

⇒ A = 60,000 × (109/100) × (109/100)

⇒ A = 6 × 109 × 109

⇒ A = 6 × 11881

⇒ A = ₹71,286

**∴ The correct answer is ₹71,286.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Effective Rate of Interest

For two successive cycles of r%, the net percentage change is given by (x + y + xy/100)%. Here, 9 + 9 + (9×9)/100 = 18.81%.

Compounding Frequencies

For **Quarterly** compounding, Rate = R/4 and n = 4T. For **Monthly** compounding, Rate = R/12 and n = 12T.

Difference between CI and SI

For 2 years (or 2 cycles), the difference between Compound Interest and Simple Interest is P(r/100)².
